parsed_response.reasoning: The diff confirms the mechanism: packages/types/Calendar.d.ts changes the `Calendar` interface to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)`, and CalendarManager now calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. The googlecalendar service adds credential-scoped selection (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`), but the office365calendar diff at line ~72 only destructures `[mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and never adds the `credentialId` parameter or credential-filtered lookup. So for an event with multiple hosts' destination calendars, Office365 will always target the first host's calendar regardless of which credential is being used — a real behavioral defect introduced/exposed by this diff (the type change is legal in TS, so it fails silently at runtime). Verifiable from the diff; confidence slightly tempered since actual wrong-calendar impact depends on multi-destination runtime data paths not fully shown.

judged_text: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:72 — `async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>` was not updated to accept the new `credentialId: number` second parameter that the diff added to the `Calendar` interface in packages/types/Calendar.d.ts, so this class silently drops the credential-scoped destination-calendar selection logic added elsewhere (e.g. googlecalendar filters `destinationCalendar` by `credentialId`, office365 still just takes `destinationCalendar[0]`), producing wrong-calendar behavior for round-robin/collective events with multiple host credentials rather than any calendar target for the correct host. Confidence 100, severity P1. Note: this does NOT produce a TypeScript compile error — verified in an isolated tsc 5.9.3 sandbox that a class method implementing fewer parameters than an interface's method signature is legal/assignable under `--strict` (TS allows discarding trailing interface parameters), so `implements Calendar` still type-checks here; the defect is a silent runtime feature-parity gap, not a build break.
